sections.h2: Who records deeds in Clinton County, Michigan?
sections.html:
The Clinton County Clerk/Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages and liens for every parcel in the county. In Clinton County the clerk and the register of deeds are one office, located at 100 E State Street, Suite 2500, in St. Johns, and the phone line is 989-224-5270.

Counter hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 5 p.m., with the office closed from noon to 1. The office asks customers to arrive by 4:30 p.m. so staff can finish a transaction properly before closing. Holiday hours can differ, so call ahead if you are driving in from the edge of the county.

The office keeps the land records, but it does not draft or change documents and gives no legal advice. It also stocks no blank deed forms. If you are selling a house in Clinton County, the title company or attorney handling your closing normally prepares the deed and sends it in for recording.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Clinton County?
sections.html:
A deed, mortgage or other instrument costs $30 to record in Clinton County, no matter how many pages it has. Michigan sets that figure by statute, and the county page for recording fees repeats it.

Clinton County recording charges that matter at a home sale
ItemChargeSource
Recording a deed or mortgage$30 per documentMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Assignment or discharge covering more than one instrument$3 for each added instrumentMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Certifying a recorded document$5MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Copies of records$1 per pageMCL 600.2567(1)(c)
Tax certificate, up to 25 legal descriptions$5, then $0.20 per added descriptionClinton County Register of Deeds

A records search by the office costs 50 cents for each year searched, with a $5 minimum, under the same statute. The county counter takes the fee when the document is left for recording.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before Clinton County will record it?
sections.html:
The deed has to meet the format rules in MCL 565.201, and the register of deeds rejects paper that does not. The county's recording requirements page lists them, and several trip people up every year.

  • Signatures must be original, with each name typed or printed beneath it, and the names must match throughout the document.
  • The first page needs a 2.5-inch top margin and at least half an inch on the other sides.
  • Print must be black, at least 10-point, on white paper of 20-pound weight or heavier, sized between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The drafter's name and address must appear, and the first line of print must name the single recordable event the paper evidences.
  • A deed signed in Michigan needs an acknowledgment before a judge, court clerk or notary.
  • No more than the last four digits of a Social Security number may appear.

The office lists missing drafter names, names not typed under signatures, an incomplete notary block and a wrong fee as the usual reasons for return. It will look over a draft against these rules before you submit it, which is cheaper than a rejected closing package. Use the legal description from the prior deed or a survey, not the shortened version on a tax bill.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when a Clinton County house sells?
sections.html:
Michigan charges two transfer taxes at recording, and the seller owes both. The state tax is $3.75 for each $500 of value or fraction of it, and the county tax is $0.55 for each $500, under MCL 207.504 and the state act at MCL 207.523.

On a $250,000 sale, the value divides into 500 units of $500. The state share comes to $1,875 and the county share to $275, a combined $2,150 that normally comes out of the seller's proceeds at the closing table. A value that does not land on an even $500 rounds up for each fraction.

  • A deed with consideration under $100 is outside both taxes.
  • A deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure is exempt from the state tax.
  • A transfer from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild is exempt from the state tax under MCL 207.526. The county act's exemption list in MCL 207.505 has no matching item, so ask the register of deeds how the county share is handled.
  • A deed that only corrects a flaw in title is exempt from both.

Any exemption has to be stated on the face of the deed. When no exemption is stated, the office collects the tax at the counter.

sections.h2: Do I need a tax certificate to record a Clinton County deed?
sections.html:
Yes, for a warranty deed. MCL 211.135 bars the register of deeds from recording a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract or an assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause until the county treasurer certifies the tax status of the parcel.

The certificate covers the five years before the date of the instrument, and it tells the buyer whether tax liens or tax titles sit against the property. Clinton County charges $5 for up to 25 legal descriptions and $0.20 for each one beyond that. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excepted from the requirement.

If you owe back property tax, ask the Clinton County Treasurer for the payoff figure before closing, so the amount can be settled from the sale proceeds and the certificate comes back clean.

sections.h2: What is the Clinton County housing market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Clinton County sits just north of Lansing and has a median owner-occupied home value of $259,500. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates also show a median household income of $88,210 and an owner-occupied housing rate of 82.2%.

The county was created in 1831 and organized in 1839, and it takes its name from DeWitt Clinton. It covers 566 square miles of land. Its cities are St. Johns, the seat, plus DeWitt and the Clinton County portions of Ovid, Lansing, East Lansing and Grand Ledge. I-69 crosses the south, US 127 runs through St. Johns and DeWitt, and M-21 passes through Fowler, St. Johns and Ovid, so commutes to Lansing are short for much of the county.

The Census Bureau counted 79,128 people in 2020 and estimates 80,432 for July 2025, a gain of 1.6%. Median gross rent is $1,092, and 197 building permits were issued in 2025. A house that needs repairs still competes with a market where owners are long settled: 89.7% of residents lived in the same home a year earlier.

sections.h2: How do I handle recording when I sell a Clinton County house for cash?
sections.html:
A cash sale records the same way as a financed one, and the closing agent normally handles it. The deed goes to the Clinton County Register of Deeds with the recording fee, a tax certificate if it is a warranty deed, and the state and county transfer tax unless an exemption is printed on the deed.

Ask the closing agent three things before you sign: who is ordering the tax certificate, whether the deed states the full consideration or attaches a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, and whether any exemption applies. Keep the recorded copy the office returns. Send a self-addressed stamped envelope if you mail original paper documents in yourself.

Also tell the local assessor about the sale. Michigan expects a Property Transfer Affidavit from the buyer within 45 days, and a seller who claimed the principal residence exemption should file to rescind it as of the closing date.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Clinton County, Michigan?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, regardless of page count. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3 for each extra instrument, and a warranty deed also needs a $5 tax certificate for up to 25 descriptions.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Clinton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. Michigan law makes the grantor liable for both the $3.75 state tax and the $0.55 county tax per $500 of value, and the amount is usually deducted from sale proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Can the register of deeds help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not draft or change documents, offers no legal advice and has no blank forms. Staff will check a draft against the recording rules, and an attorney or title company can prepare the deed itself.

faqs.q: What hours can I record in person in St. Johns?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. The office asks you to arrive by 4:30 p.m. Hours can change on holidays, so call 989-224-5270 first.

faqs.q: Why was my Clinton County deed rejected?
faqs.a: Usual causes are the wrong fee, no drafter name, names not typed under signatures, an incomplete notary certificate, margins that are too narrow, or two recordable events on one document. Fix the defect and resubmit it.
